split_rule: MOLECULE-DISJOINT, BOTH ENDPOINTS UNSEEN: a valid/test pair counts only if NEITHER molecule appears anywhere in train. Stereo- and isotope-blind key.
KNOWN_DEFECTS: D1 NO-ANCHOR RATE is 4.82%, NOT the 12.39% first reported. 61% of the original gap was a too-narrow warhead panel, not corpus contamination: alpha-ketoamide/ketoester 956 molecules (HCV/Mpro-style reversible covalent, a major class), beta-lactam 324, activated ketone 148. THE SHARPENED POINT SURVIVES: THE WARHEAD PANEL IS PART OF THE PARAM DEFINITION. Going from reachability.WARHEADS (5 patterns) to 23 moves the anchor on a large minority of the corpus and every span/flex label changes with it. STAMP THE PANEL VERSION or two corpora are not poolable.

D2 ANCHOR CORRESPONDENCE IS UNDETERMINED ON A QUARTER OF PAIRS (n=22,042 evaluable of 25,000): CLEAN (one symmetry-distinct electrophile both sides, same class) 16,517 = 74.93%; ANCHOR AMBIGUOUS (>1 on a side) 3,652 = 16.57%; ANCHOR CLASS DIFFERS between A and B 1,873 = 8.50%.

D3 REFERENCE JUMPING -- LOW RATE, CATASTROPHIC MAGNITUDE. On MCS ground truth over 1,090 clean pairs: anchor maps A->B 676 (62%); anchor OUTSIDE the MCS 157 (14.4%); A's reference ring has NO image in B 254 (23%, unanswerable); REFERENCE JUMPED 32/836 answerable = 3.83%. Label error on jumped pairs: median 4 bonds, mean 5.41, max 13 -- against a span whose OWN median is 3 and mean 2.39, with 87% of mass in 0-6. THE ERROR IS LARGER THAN THE QUANTITY: on a jumped pair the label is not a perturbation of the truth, it is unrelated to it. Rate is low enough to DROP.

D4 NEW, INDEPENDENT OF PAIRING, AND CHEAP TO FIX -- flex depends on an ARBITRARY SHORTEST PATH. Chem.GetShortestPath returns ONE path; ties are an RDKit traversal detail. Over 17,236 molecules: >1 equal-length anchor->ring path in 2,212 = 12.83%; flex CHANGES with the choice in 1,159 = 6.72%, mean spread 1.10 rotatable bonds against a flex median of 3 -- ~30% of the median value decided by traversal order. FIX: define the neighbourhood over the UNION of all shortest anchor->ring paths (deterministic, order-free). One function, no dependency on any pairing decision. DO THIS FIRST.

D5 FATAL, AND IT SUPERSEDES D3's SEVERITY ASSESSMENT. D3 quoted a 3.83% reference-jump rate on clean pairs. That number is real and USELESS: it is dominated by pairs whose span does not change, i.e. rows carrying NO training signal. Conditioned on STEERABLE rows (naive delta != 0 -- the only rows the model learns from), MCS adjudication over n=900 audited gives: mcsfail 130, UNANSWERABLE 349 (38.8% -- A's reference ring has NO image in B), answerable 421, of which REF JUMPED 160 = 38.0% OF ANSWERABLE. Only 261/900 = 29% are verifiably sound. |label error| on jumped rows: median 3, mean 3.88, max 13 -- against a span whose own median is 3. AND THE DIRECTION LABEL, WHICH IS WHAT WE TRAIN ON, SURVIVES ONLY 22/160 = 13.8%: DOWN->SAME 92, DOWN->UP 46, UP->UP 17, DOWN->DOWN 5. THE ERROR IS ASYMMETRIC: steerable rows split DOWN 51.7% / UP 48.3%, but jumped rows are 143/160 = 89% naive-DOWN, implying DOWN ~66% contaminated vs UP ~8%, an ~8x asymmetry. That is a SYSTEMATIC BIAS in the steering channel, not noise: a model trained on this learns 'decrease the span' as 'a ring got added somewhere else'. ROOT CAUSE, which is close to definitional: on rows where span CHANGES, the edit is BY CONSTRUCTION near the warhead, so the anchor lies OUTSIDE the MCS on 603/770 = 78% of them (vs 14.4% over all clean pairs). The MMP premise 'same core, same attachment, one substituent differs' -- which GUARANTEED reference correspondence -- is absent on exactly the rows that matter. All-vs-all pairing removed the thing that made the param well-defined. POOLED OVER ALL PAIRS THE CONTAMINATION IS ~2%; POOLED OVER TRAINING-SIGNAL ROWS IT IS ~38%. Anyone quoting the pooled rate concludes the corpus is safe. It is not.

ADJUDICATION_METHOD: Cheap per-molecule flags as a PREFILTER, MCS only on what they flag. The consultant's ring-system-key test alone scores PRECISION 56% (14/25) and RECALL 44% (14/32) against rdFMCS -- it over-flags on generic rings (A's reference is a benzene, B has a different benzene). So MCS IS required for adjudication, contrary to the first interim; it is the cost that must be avoided, not the instrument.
OPEN_CANDIDATE: MURCKO-SCAFFOLD reference instead of 'nearest ring system': gives the SAME delta on 95.6% of clean pairs, so it is not a different quantity -- it is the same quantity with a CONNECTED, well-defined reference object, which may make D3 structurally impossible rather than filtered. Decide on the steerable-row numbers, not the all-row numbers.
REFUTED_REMEDIES: CHEAP FRAGILE-FLAG PREFILTER IS DEAD. Flag = argmin tie across ring systems OR runner-up within 1 bond, either side. On steerable rows: FRAGILE n=28 jump rate 85.7%; NOT FRAGILE n=393 jump rate 34.6%. Highly precise, RECALL 15% -- 85% of jumps sit in rows the flag calls clean. Cannot be used as a filter, so 'prefilter cheap, MCS only the flagged' does not work.

MURCKO-SCAFFOLD REDEFINITION IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN TEST. Hypothesis was that a CONNECTED reference object removes the discontinuity. Same pairs, same MCS: Murcko gives 145/200 answerable = 72.5% jumped, |error| median 4 mean 5.19 -- WORSE than the ring reference. (Consultant's own caveat: smaller denominator, not perfectly apples-to-apples; read as 'no support for the fix', not 'twice as bad'.) Do NOT adopt it on the interim-2 suggestion.
CLEARED_NOT_HAZARDS: FUSED vs SPIRO ring-system convention: span IDENTICAL under both in 17,236/17,236 molecules (100%). The convention changes the reference's IDENTITY, never its value. Spiro in 1.62%.
MACROCYCLES: 1.03% of molecules have an SSSR ring >=12; span is 0 or 1 in 94% of those.

ANCHOR AMBIGUITY AND NEAR-TIE FRAGILITY ARE FLAT IN TC. Only classDiff scales, and it is the smallest defect. MMP guarantees a shared CORE; under a WARHEAD anchor it guarantees nothing about the warhead, and a bis-warhead molecule in an MMP pair has the same ambiguous anchor. Three of the four defects are per-MOLECULE properties of the PARAM DEFINITION that all-vs-all did not create and tighter pairing does not remove.
AND THE KILLER: AT TC>=0.9 THE STEERABLE RATE IS 0.0%. The label only exists at LOW TC. Correspondence-by-construction and a nonzero label are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. 'Go back to MMP' is closed by measurement, not by argument.

MECHANISM PREDICTS THE 7x ASYMMETRY rather than merely describing it: span goes DOWN either by shortening the linker (a real edit, rare) or by a ring appearing NEARER the warhead (common under TC>=0.4 similarity expansion). Span goes UP only by genuinely lengthening the acyclic tail, which similarity expansion cannot fake. So DOWN fills with 'a ring appeared elsewhere' and UP does not.
RECOMMENDATION_VERIFY_NOT_FILTER:
Label all pairs. Take SAME rows at face value (1.2% contaminated). MCS-adjudicate ONLY the STEERABLE rows -- ~6% of the corpus, ~90k pairs, ~1.3 s/pair single-core = ~32 core-hours, ~4 h on 8 cores. Keep REF STABLE; drop or hard-tag REF JUMPED; hard-tag UNANSWERABLE SEPARATELY (38.8% of steerable rows are not checkable at all and must not be silently merged into 'clean'). YIELD: 25,000 sampled -> 22,042 evaluable -> 16,517 clean -> 1,535 steerable -> ~29% verified stable. Scaled to 1.47M pairs: ~26,000 VERIFIED steerable span labels.
CHEAPER CUT: MCS only the DOWN rows (59.7% contaminated) and light-check UP (8.6%). Halves the bill and removes most of the bias, but leaves an 8.6% residual and a class imbalance -- state it.
THE_FREE_ALTERNATIVE_USER_DECISION: RENAME THE INSTRUCTION. If the channel is 'bring the warhead closer to / further from ring-land' -- a DESCRIPTIVE geometric relation -- then the DOWN labels are CORRECT, nothing needs dropping or verifying, and all 1,470,338 pairs survive at zero cost. What it costs is THE CLAIM: the channel can no longer be described as a LINKER edit, because ~60% of its DOWN examples are ring additions, and the stamp must say so. NOT LEGITIMATE: shipping the corpus as-is while describing it as linker steering. THIS IS A USER DECISION, not an implementation choice.
CONFIDENCE_AND_LIMITS: n=350 per stratum, n=900 pooled steerable, ONE seed, ONE 25,000-pair sample -- rates carry roughly +-5 points. rdFMCS failed or timed out on 10-17% of pairs, excluded from every denominator; IF MCS FAILURE CORRELATES WITH DISSIMILARITY IT CORRELATES WITH CONTAMINATION, SO THESE RATES ARE IF ANYTHING OPTIMISTIC. TAUTOMERS UNMEASURED -- the enumerator did not complete; a real risk for the ketoamide/enol classes and silence is NOT a clean bill. The Murcko comparison is not perfectly matched.
